description: Evaluate nodal interpolation via Neville and reusable Newton coefficients, construct/evaluate natural cubic splines, and integrate callbacks with global dyadic trapezoid or fixed-window tanh-sinh refinement. Numeric values, estimators, statuses and callback traces remain distinct observations.
forward: Evaluate nodal interpolation via Neville and reusable Newton coefficients, construct/evaluate natural cubic splines, and integrate callbacks with global dyadic trapezoid or fixed-window tanh-sinh refinement. Numeric values, estimators, statuses and callback traces remain distinct observations.

All five are std-only with no production intermodule dependencies. Neville and Newton share the unique degree<n real interpolation polynomial for identical nodes/ordinates. Natural spline shares affine data but is generally a different function for curved data. A validated interpolator can be wrapped as a deterministic quadrature callback only on a compatible query interval and with explicit handling of its Result errors.
inverse: Exclude invalid node/order success, wrong rounded divided-difference or triangular recurrence, nonfinite successful results, spline extrapolation success and wrong knot value. For quadrature exclude calls on invalid input, calls beyond budget, partial-level estimates presented as complete, or an EstimatedTolerance status inconsistent with the computed consecutive-level criterion. Real polynomial reproduction does not require bitwise equality across distinct f64 algorithms.

At fixed distinct nodes, complete real Newton coefficients identify the nodal polynomial; one query value leaves a large affine ordinate fiber. At q=0, functions x and0 both yield0. Natural curvature data alone loses the affine component. For quadrature a callback perturbation vanishing on every visited point gives the same execution while potentially changing the integral; rounded observations may merge additional inputs.
limitations: Polynomial and spline identities concern real arithmetic, not bitwise f64 agreement. Conditioning, cancellation and unsampled behavior remain unbounded. Deterministic callback is required to interpret repeated samples as one function; callback panic/resource cost and allocator failure are outside Result contracts. Tanh-sinh window [-3,3] omits tails.
Finite tests and source-derived models are not a universal proof.
state: Interpolation preserves its specified node/basis recurrence; spline uses zero endpoint second derivatives and closed-domain queries. Quadrature never exceeds caller budget, commits only complete levels, and labels consecutive-level differences as estimates rather than true-error bounds.
